entity.name: EmbeddedOS Research Foundation
entity.description: EmbeddedOS Research Foundation is a US 501(c)(3) public charity (EIN: 41-4821627) dedicated to open-source embedded operating system security. We develop and maintain eos, an MIT-licensed real-time operating system kernel written in pure C11 for ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V microcontrollers, together with the eBoot secure bootloader, the eBuild build system, the EoSim simulator and the eCAD open hardware designs. The eos repository is Experimental: its maturity record (STATUS.md) states that nothing in it has been observed to boot on hardware. Our FVRTOS programme seeks funding to add machine-checked formal verification to the kernel. We are a Linux Foundation member organization with prior funding from NLnet Foundation (EUR 150,000, NGI0 Entrust, 2024).

projects.name: eos RTOS
projects.description: eos is an MIT-licensed real-time operating system kernel written in pure C11 for ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V RV32IM microcontrollers. 15.8 KB flash and 26.0 KB RAM on Cortex-M4, with descriptors for 84 boards. The repository is Experimental and its maturity record (STATUS.md) reports no board-level evidence: the ARM artifacts cross-compile clean but have never been executed. The FVRTOS project seeks funding to produce the first machine-checked formally verified open-source RTOS kernel; no proofs are complete today. Prior funding: NLnet Foundation NGI0 Entrust EUR 150,000 (2024). License: MIT.

projects.name: eBoot Secure Bootloader
projects.description: A secure two-stage bootloader for embedded systems with hardware-backed cryptographic verification, supporting AES and SHA-256/512.

projects.name: eBuild Build System
projects.description: A build system supporting 171 microcontrollers across multiple architectures, enabling cross-platform embedded development with a single unified toolchain.

projects.name: EoSim Simulator
projects.description: A multi-platform simulator supporting 153 embedded platforms, enabling development and testing without physical hardware.

projects.name: eCAD Open Hardware Designs
projects.description: Open-source hardware designs covering 125 product lines, 15 development boards, and 4 health monitoring devices. All designs are freely available for modification and manufacture.
